item.title: US Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed launches 'Habibi PAC' days after historic election win
item.description: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee (PAC) named 'Habibi PAC', days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate, Al Jazeera reported.
item.content:encoded:
US Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed launches 'Habibi PAC' days after historic election win Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee (PAC) named 'Habibi PAC', days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate, Al Jazeera reported. ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 21:32 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 21:32 IST

Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee (PAC) named 'Habibi PAC', days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate, Al Jazeera reported. According to Al Jazeera, citing a filing submitted to the Federal Election Commission (FEC) on Thursday, Habibi PAC has been registered as a leadership PAC sponsored by El-Sayed. Such committees operate separately from a politician's own election campaign and are used to raise and spend funds in support of other political candidates and political activities. The name 'Habibi', an Arabic term of endearment meaning 'my dear' or 'my beloved', is a phrase El-Sayed frequently used during his election campaign. He also used the expression while addressing US Vice President JD Vance during his victory speech in Detroit, saying, "JD, habibi, there is this delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January." El-Sayed is among several newly elected Democratic lawmakers who have registered leadership PACs following Tuesday's election, according to FEC filings. Others include Arizona Congressman-elect Amish Shah, who registered 'PACStreet Boy', Iowa Senator-elect Josh Turek, who launched 'WheelPAC', and North Carolina Senator-elect Roy Cooper, who registered 'One NC PAC', as reported by Al Jazeera. According to Al Jazeera, citing OpenSecrets, leadership PACs are often used by ambitious lawmakers to build influence among their colleagues and strengthen their prospects of securing party leadership positions or committee chairmanships. They typically contribute to other lawmakers, political parties and political committees. During the 2024 election cycle, leadership PACs contributed USD 79.3 million to federal candidates. While most of the contributions went to Republican candidates, a Democratic leadership PAC emerged as the largest individual donor, Al Jazeera reported, citing OpenSecrets. El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, defeated Republican candidate Mike Rogers following a campaign in which US President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Senator Ted Cruz questioned his loyalty, called him a "jihadist" and attempted to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood movement without providing evidence. Getting money out of politics was among El-Sayed's central campaign pledges. During his victory speech, he highlighted the significance of his electoral success, saying that in a contest between money and the people, "the many can win". His victory came amid the most expensive midterm election on record. According to Al Jazeera, an analysis of FEC data by OpenSecrets noted that total spending in the election cycle is expected to reach USD 11.9 billion, compared with USD 8.9 billion in 2022. Outside spending, largely driven by super PACs, is projected to reach USD 3.9 billion, marking an 85 per cent increase from the 2022 midterm elections. Meanwhile, so-called dark money contributions from donors whose identities are not disclosed have already reached at least USD 1.47 billion, surpassing the previous record of USD 1.35 billion set during the 2024 election cycle, which also included the presidential race. According to Al Jazeera, OpenSecrets found that conservative groups outspent liberal groups by approximately USD 360 million in outside spending, while Democratic candidates were expected to outspend their Republican counterparts by around USD 800 million. Political action committees, or PACs, are organisations that raise and spend money to support or oppose candidates for public office. Leadership PACs, in particular, allow elected officials and lawmakers to support other candidates and political organisations independently of their own campaign committees. (ANI)

item.description: Leaders of several major political parties in Balochistan have announced a province-wide shutdown strike on November 19, followed by demonstrations at all district headquarters, accusing the ...
item.content:encoded:
Balochistan parties announce province-wide shutdown amid deepening crisis Leaders of several major political parties in Balochistan have announced a province-wide shutdown strike on November 19, followed by demonstrations at all district headquarters, accusing the government of failing to address the province’s worsening political, security and economic crises, as reported by The Express Tribune. ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 17:38 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 17:38 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Leaders of several major political parties in Balochistan have announced a province-wide shutdown strike on November 19, followed by demonstrations at all district headquarters, accusing the government of failing to address the province’s worsening political, security and economic crises, as reported by The Express Tribune. According to The Express Tribune, the decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP) at the Quetta Press Club, chaired by ANP provincial president Asghar Khan Achakzai. Participating parties agreed to turn their joint political and democratic struggle into a coordinated movement against what they described as growing public grievances. The leaders also announced a provincial-level meeting on November 26 to determine the next phase of their campaign. An all-parties conference will subsequently be convened in the first week of December to present Balochistan’s pressing concerns before the national leadership. Representatives of the National Party, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, Pashtunkhwa National Awami Party and other political groups attended the gathering. In a joint declaration, the participating parties described the situation in Balochistan as alarming and unacceptable, highlighting persistent insecurity, terrorism, extremism, armed group activities, targeted killings and kidnappings for ransom. They also raised concerns over the unresolved issue of missing persons, unemployment, economic deterioration and difficulties faced by transporters and passengers travelling on national highways. The declaration further blamed the closure of trade and transit routes with Afghanistan and Iran for severely disrupting economic activity across the province. Political leaders also highlighted the impact of soaring inflation, prolonged electricity and gas outages, petroleum levies and restrictions on essential agricultural supplies, including urea fertiliser, as cited by The Express Tribune. They maintained that these measures have adversely affected agriculture, trade, industries and employment. The parties launched a strong attack on the provincial and federal governments, accusing them of failing to protect citizens, maintain law and order, safeguard natural resources and restore economic stability, as reported by The Express Tribune. (ANI)

item.title: Pakistan forces under fire after missing Baloch youth found dead in Gwadar amid enforced disappearances
item.description: The body of a young man allegedly abducted by Pakistani forces was found in Gwadar after a year. Meanwhile, families in Turbat demanded information about missing relatives, and the Voice for Baloch ...
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan forces under fire after missing Baloch youth found dead in Gwadar amid enforced disappearances The body of a young man allegedly abducted by Pakistani forces was found in Gwadar after a year. Meanwhile, families in Turbat demanded information about missing relatives, and the Voice for Baloch Missing Persons continued protests in Quetta, urging authorities to ensure the safe recovery of missing individuals. ANI | Updated: 07-11-2026 14:34 IST | Created: 07-11-2026 14:34 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Allegations of enforced disappearances and custodial abuses have intensified concerns over Pakistan’s treatment of Baloch civilians after the body of a young man, allegedly abducted by Pakistani security forces, was discovered in Gwadar district, as reported by The Balochistan Post. According to The Balochistan Post, the deceased, identified as Ahmed, son of Gwahram Baloch, was reportedly detained by security personnel in Gwadar’s Shadi Kaur locality on October 5, 2025. He was subsequently moved to an undisclosed location. His body was recovered on October 19, 2026, raising further questions about the circumstances surrounding his disappearance and death. Meanwhile, three families in Turbat, Kech district, have demanded information about relatives allegedly taken away by Pakistani forces. Security personnel allegedly detained Talau, son of Naguman; Muhammad Hayat, son of Babul; and Charshambay, son of Shambay, from Askani Absar at approximately 8 pm on October 24. The families stated that a vehicle and personal possessions were also confiscated during the operation. Despite repeated appeals, the whereabouts of the three men remain unknown. Pir Jan, Talau’s son, said relatives had contacted administrative authorities and publicised the disappearances but received no meaningful response. The families urged Kech’s deputy commissioner, district police officer and Makran commissioner to intervene immediately. The Voice for Baloch Missing Persons (VBMP) continued its longstanding demonstration outside the Quetta Press Club, marking its 6,410th day of protest. Journalist Saifullah Sarparah and Comrade Manzoor Baloch visited the demonstration site and expressed solidarity with affected families, as highlighted by The Balochistan Post. VBMP chairman Nasrullah Baloch highlighted the devastating emotional, psychological and social consequences of enforced disappearances, stressing that entire households suffer when their friends and relatives vanish without explanation. Nasrullah appealed to Pakistan’s government and institutional leadership to prioritise humanitarian considerations and ensure the safe recovery of missing individuals, as reported by The Balochistan Post. (ANI)
